newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo Nikkei expected to test 19,000.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo Nikkei expected to test 19,000.

text.p: The weak yen and financial reform proposals -- factors blamed for sending Tokyo shares plummeting earlier -- are now being seen as positives in a newly revived market that could well push higher in the week ahead, traders said.

The Nikkei index of 225 leading companies, which climbed 4.8 percent to end at 18,722.00, may push through the 19,000 barrier this week as the buying seen in blue-chip issues is likely to extend to other companies.
Brokers said the weak yen, previously blamed for the market's downturn and seen as a sign of a new Japanese economic crisis, is now seen as giving a healthy boost to the bottom line.
"The market's eye is turning to favorable effects from the yen's depreciation," said Masaaki Higashida, deputy general manager at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
In addition, financial reforms being pushed by the government are seen as aiding a much needed shakeout in corporate Japan.
Higashida said he expected the key stock index to range between 18,500 and 19,500 this week.

"The weak yen provided positive incentives to the market," said Tim Hayashida, strategist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc, adding that it was expected to help a broader range of stocks, including those of medium-sized firms.

Indeed, stocks were supported on Friday by catch-up buying in lower-priced shares, such as in the steel sector Telecommunication shares also helped the rise. But the upside was limited by profit-taking in high-priced blue-chip shares, which had rallied recently.
Hiroyuki Nakai, chief investment strategist at Nikko Securities Co Ltd, said he expected the Nikkei 225 to head gradually higher to the 19,000-20,000 range by the end of this financial year in March.

"Despite several negative factors, the downside risk is limited in the new fiscal year (starting April) and the 17,000 level will likely be a bottom for the Nikkei 225," said Chisato Haganuma, a strategist of Nomura Research Institute.
In the next several months, he added, a Nikkei 225 average level of 17,000 to 20,000 would be appropriate.

Structural reforms are already under way among private companies, especially in the wage system of some major companies, and the fragility of Japan's financial system, another market concern, has already been discounted in the market, Haganuma said.
Last weekend, financial authorities endorsed a stable dollar at the Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Berlin.
